summary: Passaic Co., NJ tower built on Windbeam Mountain in 1920; moved in 1971 and 1983, and now stands at Ramapo Mountain State Forest, not on the original summit.

facts.design: Steel angle-iron tower with a one-room penthouse for the warden (1931 newspaper description); the moved tower is an Aermotor, LS-40 or LS-42 per the two registers, with a 7'x7' cab
facts.status_note: The Windbeam Mountain site is gone. The tower was moved and has stood at Ramapo Mountain State Forest since 1983, as the Ramapo Lookout (US 45, NJ 2).
facts.agency: NJ Forest Fire Service administers the moved tower (NHLR); North Jersey District Water Supply is listed for the original site (FFLOS)

events.note: Built with funds from the Ringwood Company; the state annual report says in service from June 15, 1920
Moved off Windbeam Mountain. The Windbeam entry says Pierson Ridge; the Pierson Ridge entry says Ringwood State Park, with National Guard and volunteer labor
Remains moved to Ramapo Mountain State Forest and rebuilt from 1983 per the Pierson Ridge entry; NHLR says present location since 1983
NHLR visit report dated May 1, 2007 for the Ramapo Lookout answers yes to Staffed?

notes_for_editor: The record's status 'gone' fits only the Windbeam Mountain site. The same tower is the Ramapo Lookout (NHLR US 45, NJ 2; Wikipedia 'Ramapo Station'), standing at Ramapo Mountain State Forest since 1983; check for a separate Ramapo record and link them. Sources disagree on several points: (1) height: 45 ft in the 1920 report (matches the record's 13.7 m), 50 ft in a 1923 article and on Wikipedia, 60 ft in the Pierson Ridge entry; (2) model: LS-40 (NHLR) vs LS-42 (Pierson Ridge); (3) the 1971 destination: Pierson Ridge (Windbeam entry) vs Ringwood State Park (Pierson entry); (4) fate: Pierson says vandals destroyed the tower and it was rebuilt from remains, while the Windbeam entry says it moved and is in active use. The story records both. The vandalism has no date, so it is not an event. Staffing is from a May 2007 NHLR visit report and may be stale. No source describes the public access or climbing status of the Ramapo tower, and none describes what remains on Windbeam Mountain. The record's 1971 'removed' event is left as is. An Oakland NJ history post about a stone tower on Skyline Drive was checked and is a different structure, so it is not used. Budget: one websearch.py query plus about 10 page reads, over the 8-read budget, because the three register pages and the Wikipedia list needed checking against each other.
